title: Multi-Step Reasoning with Large Language Models, a Survey
explain_beginner: This survey looks at how large language models handle problems that need several reasoning steps. It says a method called chain of thought helped these models do much better on basic reasoning tests. The authors organize the field by how reasoning is produced, checked, and guided. They report that progress has moved past simple math word problems into logic, games, and robotics, sometimes by writing code that outside tools run. The paper matters because it gives a clear map of what these systems can do and what questions remain, helping readers understand both promise and limits.
explain_business: This survey gives leaders a structured way to think about systems that solve problems through several reasoning steps. It shows that large language models can now handle more than simple math word problems, including logic, games, and robotics, sometimes by creating code for external tools to run. The authors organize how such reasoning is produced, checked, and guided, which the editor notes can support audit test design. In practice, this can inform decisions about how to structure evaluations and controls for multi step reasoning, and where to focus audit tests.
explain_practitioner: The authors review multi step reasoning in large language models. They build a taxonomy for how such reasoning is generated, evaluated, and controlled. The paper covers core methods and open problems, then proposes a near term research agenda. It notes that chain of thought is an in context learning approach that improved performance on reasoning benchmarks. The review finds that multi step methods now address logic, combinatorial games, and robotics, sometimes by first producing code that external tools execute. It also reports that many methods use reinforcement learning for finetuning, external optimization loops, in context reinforcement learning, and self reflection.
